## Overview

Summary of dataset and variables
This dataset provides population estimates for the local authorities in Wales, the English regions and the UK countries for the period from 1991 onwards by sex and single year of age.

It should be noted that for mid-2020 there are some definitional changes, particularly affecting the migration components, compared with mid-2019 population estimates data and it is advised users read the Quality and Methodology Information section on the Office for National Statistics website.

For Wales, England and Northern Ireland, the mid-2021 population estimates are the first population estimates to be based on the 2021 censuses for these countries. For Scotland, the census was moved to 2022. The mid-2022 population estimates are the first population estimates to be based on the 2022 Census for Scotland.

On 23 November 2023, the data set from 2012 to 2020 for Wales and England were rebased to be consistent with the results of Census 2021. Northern Ireland published rebased 2012 to 2020 data on 29 June 2023. Scotland published rebased 2012 to 2020 data on 9 July 2024.

On 29 July 2026 estimates for mid-2022, mid-2023 and mid-2024 were revised by the ONS to account for updated estimates of international migration for Wales and England.

Internal migration estimates for mid-2023 have been produced using a different method to previous years, following a change to the variables available in the Higher Education Statistics Agency data.

Data collection or calculation
The Office for National Statistics (ONS) publish mid-year population estimates for Wales and England as a whole. Further information on how the data are calculated can be found on the ONS' website. A link can be found in the weblink section.

## Overview

Summary of dataset and variables
This dataset provides population estimates for the local authorities in Wales, the English regions and the UK countries for the period from 1991 onwards by sex and single year of age.

It should be noted that for mid-2020 there are some definitional changes, particularly affecting the migration components, compared with mid-2019 population estimates data and it is advised users read the Quality and Methodology Information section on the Office for National Statistics website.

For Wales, England and Northern Ireland, the mid-2021 population estimates are the first population estimates to be based on the 2021 censuses for these countries. For Scotland, the census was moved to 2022. The mid-2022 population estimates are the first population estimates to be based on the 2022 Census for Scotland.

On 23 November 2023, the data set from 2012 to 2020 for Wales and England were rebased to be consistent with the results of Census 2021. Northern Ireland published rebased 2012 to 2020 data on 29 June 2023. Scotland published rebased 2012 to 2020 data on 9 July 2024.

On 29 July 2026 estimates for mid-2022, mid-2023 and mid-2024 were revised by the ONS to account for updated estimates of international migration for Wales and England.

Internal migration estimates for mid-2023 have been produced using a different method to previous years, following a change to the variables available in the Higher Education Statistics Agency data.

Data collection or calculation
The Office for National Statistics (ONS) publish mid-year population estimates for Wales and England as a whole. Further information on how the data are calculated can be found on the ONS' website. A link can be found in the weblink section.

Statistical quality
The Office for National Statistics (ONS) publish mid-year population estimates for Wales and England as a whole. Further information on statistical quality can be found on the ONS' website. A link can be found in the weblink section.

## Overview

Summary of dataset and variables
This dataset provides population estimates for the local authorities in Wales, the English regions and the UK countries for the period from 1991 onwards by sex and single year of age.

It should be noted that for mid-2020 there are some definitional changes, particularly affecting the migration components, compared with mid-2019 population estimates data and it is advised users read the Quality and Methodology Information section on the Office for National Statistics website.

For Wales, England and Northern Ireland, the mid-2021 population estimates are the first population estimates to be based on the 2021 censuses for these countries. For Scotland, the census was moved to 2022. The mid-2022 population estimates are the first population estimates to be based on the 2022 Census for Scotland.

On 23 November 2023, the data set from 2012 to 2020 for Wales and England were rebased to be consistent with the results of Census 2021. Northern Ireland published rebased 2012 to 2020 data on 29 June 2023. Scotland published rebased 2012 to 2020 data on 9 July 2024.

On 29 July 2026 estimates for mid-2022, mid-2023 and mid-2024 were revised by the ONS to account for updated estimates of international migration for Wales and England.

Internal migration estimates for mid-2023 have been produced using a different method to previous years, following a change to the variables available in the Higher Education Statistics Agency data.

Data collection or calculation
The Office for National Statistics (ONS) publish mid-year population estimates for Wales and England as a whole. Further information on how the data are calculated can be found on the ONS' website. A link can be found in the weblink section.

Statistical quality
The Office for National Statistics (ONS) publish mid-year population estimates for Wales and England as a whole. Further information on statistical quality can be found on the ONS' website. A link can be found in the weblink section.

## Overview

Summary of dataset and variables
This dataset provides population estimates for the local authorities in Wales, the English regions and the UK countries for the period from 1991 onwards by sex and single year of age.

It should be noted that for mid-2020 there are some definitional changes, particularly affecting the migration components, compared with mid-2019 population estimates data and it is advised users read the Quality and Methodology Information section on the Office for National Statistics website.

For Wales, England and Northern Ireland, the mid-2021 population estimates are the first population estimates to be based on the 2021 censuses for these countries. For Scotland, the census was moved to 2022. The mid-2022 population estimates are the first population estimates to be based on the 2022 Census for Scotland.

On 23 November 2023, the data set from 2012 to 2020 for Wales and England were rebased to be consistent with the results of Census 2021. Northern Ireland published rebased 2012 to 2020 data on 29 June 2023. Scotland published rebased 2012 to 2020 data on 9 July 2024.

On 29 July 2026 estimates for mid-2022, mid-2023 and mid-2024 were revised by the ONS to account for updated estimates of international migration for Wales and England.

Internal migration estimates for mid-2023 have been produced using a different method to previous years, following a change to the variables available in the Higher Education Statistics Agency data.

Data collection or calculation
The Office for National Statistics (ONS) publish mid-year population estimates for Wales and England as a whole. Further information on how the data are calculated can be found on the ONS' website. A link can be found in the weblink section.

Statistical quality
The Office for National Statistics (ONS) publish mid-year population estimates for Wales and England as a whole. Further information on statistical quality can be found on the ONS' website. A link can be found in the weblink section.

## Overview

Summary of dataset and variables
This dataset provides population estimates for the local authorities in Wales, the English regions and the UK countries for the period from 1991 onwards by sex and single year of age.

It should be noted that for mid-2020 there are some definitional changes, particularly affecting the migration components, compared with mid-2019 population estimates data and it is advised users read the Quality and Methodology Information section on the Office for National Statistics website.

For Wales, England and Northern Ireland, the mid-2021 population estimates are the first population estimates to be based on the 2021 censuses for these countries. For Scotland, the census was moved to 2022. The mid-2022 population estimates are the first population estimates to be based on the 2022 Census for Scotland.

On 23 November 2023, the data set from 2012 to 2020 for Wales and England were rebased to be consistent with the results of Census 2021. Northern Ireland published rebased 2012 to 2020 data on 29 June 2023. Scotland published rebased 2012 to 2020 data on 9 July 2024.

On 29 July 2026 estimates for mid-2022, mid-2023 and mid-2024 were revised by the ONS to account for updated estimates of international migration for Wales and England.

Internal migration estimates for mid-2023 have been produced using a different method to previous years, following a change to the variables available in the Higher Education Statistics Agency data.

Data collection or calculation
The Office for National Statistics (ONS) publish mid-year population estimates for Wales and England as a whole. Further information on how the data are calculated can be found on the ONS' website. A link can be found in the weblink section.

Statistical quality
The Office for National Statistics (ONS) publish mid-year population estimates for Wales and England as a whole. Further information on statistical quality can be found on the ONS' website. A link can be found in the weblink section.

## Overview

Summary of dataset and variables
This dataset provides population estimates for the local authorities in Wales, the English regions and the UK countries for the period from 1991 onwards by sex and single year of age.

It should be noted that for mid-2020 there are some definitional changes, particularly affecting the migration components, compared with mid-2019 population estimates data and it is advised users read the Quality and Methodology Information section on the Office for National Statistics website.

For Wales, England and Northern Ireland, the mid-2021 population estimates are the first population estimates to be based on the 2021 censuses for these countries. For Scotland, the census was moved to 2022. The mid-2022 population estimates are the first population estimates to be based on the 2022 Census for Scotland.

On 23 November 2023, the data set from 2012 to 2020 for Wales and England were rebased to be consistent with the results of Census 2021. Northern Ireland published rebased 2012 to 2020 data on 29 June 2023. Scotland published rebased 2012 to 2020 data on 9 July 2024.

On 29 July 2026 estimates for mid-2022, mid-2023 and mid-2024 were revised by the ONS to account for updated estimates of international migration for Wales and England.

Internal migration estimates for mid-2023 have been produced using a different method to previous years, following a change to the variables available in the Higher Education Statistics Agency data.

Data collection or calculation
The Office for National Statistics (ONS) publish mid-year population estimates for Wales and England as a whole. Further information on how the data are calculated can be found on the ONS' website. A link can be found in the weblink section.

Statistical quality
The Office for National Statistics (ONS) publish mid-year population estimates for Wales and England as a whole. Further information on statistical quality can be found on the ONS' website. A link can be found in the weblink section.

## Main information

Designation Accredited official statistics

Data provider Office for National Statistics (ONS)

Data source Mid-year population estimates

Dataset ID 82d9faea-b515-41cd-aedb-8f4594f66ce5

## Overview

Summary of dataset and variables
This dataset provides population estimates for the local authorities in Wales, the English regions and the UK countries for the period from 1991 onwards by sex and single year of age.

It should be noted that for mid-2020 there are some definitional changes, particularly affecting the migration components, compared with mid-2019 population estimates data and it is advised users read the Quality and Methodology Information section on the Office for National Statistics website.

For Wales, England and Northern Ireland, the mid-2021 population estimates are the first population estimates to be based on the 2021 censuses for these countries. For Scotland, the census was moved to 2022. The mid-2022 population estimates are the first population estimates to be based on the 2022 Census for Scotland.

On 23 November 2023, the data set from 2012 to 2020 for Wales and England were rebased to be consistent with the results of Census 2021. Northern Ireland published rebased 2012 to 2020 data on 29 June 2023. Scotland published rebased 2012 to 2020 data on 9 July 2024.

On 29 July 2026 estimates for mid-2022, mid-2023 and mid-2024 were revised by the ONS to account for updated estimates of international migration for Wales and England.

Internal migration estimates for mid-2023 have been produced using a different method to previous years, following a change to the variables available in the Higher Education Statistics Agency data.

Data collection or calculation
The Office for National Statistics (ONS) publish mid-year population estimates for Wales and England as a whole. Further information on how the data are calculated can be found on the ONS' website. A link can be found in the weblink section.

Statistical quality
The Office for National Statistics (ONS) publish mid-year population estimates for Wales and England as a whole. Further information on statistical quality can be found on the ONS' website. A link can be found in the weblink section.

## Overview

Summary of dataset and variables
This dataset provides population estimates for the local authorities in Wales, the English regions and the UK countries for the period from 1991 onwards by sex and single year of age.

It should be noted that for mid-2020 there are some definitional changes, particularly affecting the migration components, compared with mid-2019 population estimates data and it is advised users read the Quality and Methodology Information section on the Office for National Statistics website.

For Wales, England and Northern Ireland, the mid-2021 population estimates are the first population estimates to be based on the 2021 censuses for these countries. For Scotland, the census was moved to 2022. The mid-2022 population estimates are the first population estimates to be based on the 2022 Census for Scotland.

On 23 November 2023, the data set from 2012 to 2020 for Wales and England were rebased to be consistent with the results of Census 2021. Northern Ireland published rebased 2012 to 2020 data on 29 June 2023. Scotland published rebased 2012 to 2020 data on 9 July 2024.

On 29 July 2026 estimates for mid-2022, mid-2023 and mid-2024 were revised by the ONS to account for updated estimates of international migration for Wales and England.

Internal migration estimates for mid-2023 have been produced using a different method to previous years, following a change to the variables available in the Higher Education Statistics Agency data.

Data collection or calculation
The Office for National Statistics (ONS) publish mid-year population estimates for Wales and England as a whole. Further information on how the data are calculated can be found on the ONS' website. A link can be found in the weblink section.

## Overview

Summary of dataset and variables
This dataset provides population estimates for the local authorities in Wales, the English regions and the UK countries for the period from 1991 onwards by sex and single year of age.

It should be noted that for mid-2020 there are some definitional changes, particularly affecting the migration components, compared with mid-2019 population estimates data and it is advised users read the Quality and Methodology Information section on the Office for National Statistics website.

For Wales, England and Northern Ireland, the mid-2021 population estimates are the first population estimates to be based on the 2021 censuses for these countries. For Scotland, the census was moved to 2022. The mid-2022 population estimates are the first population estimates to be based on the 2022 Census for Scotland.

On 23 November 2023, the data set from 2012 to 2020 for Wales and England were rebased to be consistent with the results of Census 2021. Northern Ireland published rebased 2012 to 2020 data on 29 June 2023. Scotland published rebased 2012 to 2020 data on 9 July 2024.

On 29 July 2026 estimates for mid-2022, mid-2023 and mid-2024 were revised by the ONS to account for updated estimates of international migration for Wales and England.

Internal migration estimates for mid-2023 have been produced using a different method to previous years, following a change to the variables available in the Higher Education Statistics Agency data.

Data collection or calculation
The Office for National Statistics (ONS) publish mid-year population estimates for Wales and England as a whole. Further information on how the data are calculated can be found on the ONS' website. A link can be found in the weblink section.

Statistical quality
The Office for National Statistics (ONS) publish mid-year population estimates for Wales and England as a whole. Further information on statistical quality can be found on the ONS' website. A link can be found in the weblink section.

## Overview

Summary of dataset and variables
This dataset provides population estimates for the local authorities in Wales, the English regions and the UK countries for the period from 1991 onwards by sex and single year of age.

It should be noted that for mid-2020 there are some definitional changes, particularly affecting the migration components, compared with mid-2019 population estimates data and it is advised users read the Quality and Methodology Information section on the Office for National Statistics website.

For Wales, England and Northern Ireland, the mid-2021 population estimates are the first population estimates to be based on the 2021 censuses for these countries. For Scotland, the census was moved to 2022. The mid-2022 population estimates are the first population estimates to be based on the 2022 Census for Scotland.

On 23 November 2023, the data set from 2012 to 2020 for Wales and England were rebased to be consistent with the results of Census 2021. Northern Ireland published rebased 2012 to 2020 data on 29 June 2023. Scotland published rebased 2012 to 2020 data on 9 July 2024.

On 29 July 2026 estimates for mid-2022, mid-2023 and mid-2024 were revised by the ONS to account for updated estimates of international migration for Wales and England.

Internal migration estimates for mid-2023 have been produced using a different method to previous years, following a change to the variables available in the Higher Education Statistics Agency data.

Data collection or calculation

Designation Accredited official statistics

Data source Mid-year population estimates

Dataset ID 82d9faea-b515-41cd-aedb-8f4594f66ce5

## Overview

Summary of dataset and variables
This dataset provides population estimates for the local authorities in Wales, the English regions and the UK countries for the period from 1991 onwards by sex and single year of age.

It should be noted that for mid-2020 there are some definitional changes, particularly affecting the migration components, compared with mid-2019 population estimates data and it is advised users read the Quality and Methodology Information section on the Office for National Statistics website.

For Wales, England and Northern Ireland, the mid-2021 population estimates are the first population estimates to be based on the 2021 censuses for these countries. For Scotland, the census was moved to 2022. The mid-2022 population estimates are the first population estimates to be based on the 2022 Census for Scotland.

On 23 November 2023, the data set from 2012 to 2020 for Wales and England were rebased to be consistent with the results of Census 2021. Northern Ireland published rebased 2012 to 2020 data on 29 June 2023. Scotland published rebased 2012 to 2020 data on 9 July 2024.

On 29 July 2026 estimates for mid-2022, mid-2023 and mid-2024 were revised by the ONS to account for updated estimates of international migration for Wales and England.

Internal migration estimates for mid-2023 have been produced using a different method to previous years, following a change to the variables available in the Higher Education Statistics Agency data.

Data collection or calculation
The Office for National Statistics (ONS) publish mid-year population estimates for Wales and England as a whole. Further information on how the data are calculated can be found on the ONS' website. A link can be found in the weblink section.

Statistical quality
The Office for National Statistics (ONS) publish mid-year population estimates for Wales and England as a whole. Further information on statistical quality can be found on the ONS' website. A link can be found in the weblink section.

## Main information

Data provider Office for National Statistics (ONS)

Data source Mid-year population estimates

Dataset ID 82d9faea-b515-41cd-aedb-8f4594f66ce5

## Overview

Summary of dataset and variables
This dataset provides population estimates for the local authorities in Wales, the English regions and the UK countries for the period from 1991 onwards by sex and single year of age.

It should be noted that for mid-2020 there are some definitional changes, particularly affecting the migration components, compared with mid-2019 population estimates data and it is advised users read the Quality and Methodology Information section on the Office for National Statistics website.

For Wales, England and Northern Ireland, the mid-2021 population estimates are the first population estimates to be based on the 2021 censuses for these countries. For Scotland, the census was moved to 2022. The mid-2022 population estimates are the first population estimates to be based on the 2022 Census for Scotland.

On 23 November 2023, the data set from 2012 to 2020 for Wales and England were rebased to be consistent with the results of Census 2021. Northern Ireland published rebased 2012 to 2020 data on 29 June 2023. Scotland published rebased 2012 to 2020 data on 9 July 2024.

On 29 July 2026 estimates for mid-2022, mid-2023 and mid-2024 were revised by the ONS to account for updated estimates of international migration for Wales and England.

Internal migration estimates for mid-2023 have been produced using a different method to previous years, following a change to the variables available in the Higher Education Statistics Agency data.

Data collection or calculation
The Office for National Statistics (ONS) publish mid-year population estimates for Wales and England as a whole. Further information on how the data are calculated can be found on the ONS' website. A link can be found in the weblink section.

Statistical quality
The Office for National Statistics (ONS) publish mid-year population estimates for Wales and England as a whole. Further information on statistical quality can be found on the ONS' website. A link can be found in the weblink section.

## Overview

Summary of dataset and variables
This dataset provides population estimates for the local authorities in Wales, the English regions and the UK countries for the period from 1991 onwards by sex and single year of age.

It should be noted that for mid-2020 there are some definitional changes, particularly affecting the migration components, compared with mid-2019 population estimates data and it is advised users read the Quality and Methodology Information section on the Office for National Statistics website.

For Wales, England and Northern Ireland, the mid-2021 population estimates are the first population estimates to be based on the 2021 censuses for these countries. For Scotland, the census was moved to 2022. The mid-2022 population estimates are the first population estimates to be based on the 2022 Census for Scotland.

On 23 November 2023, the data set from 2012 to 2020 for Wales and England were rebased to be consistent with the results of Census 2021. Northern Ireland published rebased 2012 to 2020 data on 29 June 2023. Scotland published rebased 2012 to 2020 data on 9 July 2024.

On 29 July 2026 estimates for mid-2022, mid-2023 and mid-2024 were revised by the ONS to account for updated estimates of international migration for Wales and England.

Internal migration estimates for mid-2023 have been produced using a different method to previous years, following a change to the variables available in the Higher Education Statistics Agency data.

Data collection or calculation
The Office for National Statistics (ONS) publish mid-year population estimates for Wales and England as a whole. Further information on how the data are calculated can be found on the ONS' website. A link can be found in the weblink section.

Statistical quality
The Office for National Statistics (ONS) publish mid-year population estimates for Wales and England as a whole. Further information on statistical quality can be found on the ONS' website. A link can be found in the weblink section.

## Overview

Summary of dataset and variables
This dataset provides population estimates for the local authorities in Wales, the English regions and the UK countries for the period from 1991 onwards by sex and single year of age.

It should be noted that for mid-2020 there are some definitional changes, particularly affecting the migration components, compared with mid-2019 population estimates data and it is advised users read the Quality and Methodology Information section on the Office for National Statistics website.

For Wales, England and Northern Ireland, the mid-2021 population estimates are the first population estimates to be based on the 2021 censuses for these countries. For Scotland, the census was moved to 2022. The mid-2022 population estimates are the first population estimates to be based on the 2022 Census for Scotland.

On 23 November 2023, the data set from 2012 to 2020 for Wales and England were rebased to be consistent with the results of Census 2021. Northern Ireland published rebased 2012 to 2020 data on 29 June 2023. Scotland published rebased 2012 to 2020 data on 9 July 2024.

On 29 July 2026 estimates for mid-2022, mid-2023 and mid-2024 were revised by the ONS to account for updated estimates of international migration for Wales and England.

Internal migration estimates for mid-2023 have been produced using a different method to previous years, following a change to the variables available in the Higher Education Statistics Agency data.

Data collection or calculation
The Office for National Statistics (ONS) publish mid-year population estimates for Wales and England as a whole. Further information on how the data are calculated can be found on the ONS' website. A link can be found in the weblink section.

Statistical quality
The Office for National Statistics (ONS) publish mid-year population estimates for Wales and England as a whole. Further information on statistical quality can be found on the ONS' website. A link can be found in the weblink section.

## Overview

Summary of dataset and variables
This dataset provides population estimates for the local authorities in Wales, the English regions and the UK countries for the period from 1991 onwards by sex and single year of age.

It should be noted that for mid-2020 there are some definitional changes, particularly affecting the migration components, compared with mid-2019 population estimates data and it is advised users read the Quality and Methodology Information section on the Office for National Statistics website.

For Wales, England and Northern Ireland, the mid-2021 population estimates are the first population estimates to be based on the 2021 censuses for these countries. For Scotland, the census was moved to 2022. The mid-2022 population estimates are the first population estimates to be based on the 2022 Census for Scotland.

On 23 November 2023, the data set from 2012 to 2020 for Wales and England were rebased to be consistent with the results of Census 2021. Northern Ireland published rebased 2012 to 2020 data on 29 June 2023. Scotland published rebased 2012 to 2020 data on 9 July 2024.

On 29 July 2026 estimates for mid-2022, mid-2023 and mid-2024 were revised by the ONS to account for updated estimates of international migration for Wales and England.

Internal migration estimates for mid-2023 have been produced using a different method to previous years, following a change to the variables available in the Higher Education Statistics Agency data.

Data collection or calculation
The Office for National Statistics (ONS) publish mid-year population estimates for Wales and England as a whole. Further information on how the data are calculated can be found on the ONS' website. A link can be found in the weblink section.

Statistical quality
The Office for National Statistics (ONS) publish mid-year population estimates for Wales and England as a whole. Further information on statistical quality can be found on the ONS' website. A link can be found in the weblink section.

## Overview

Summary of dataset and variables
This dataset provides population estimates for the local authorities in Wales, the English regions and the UK countries for the period from 1991 onwards by sex and single year of age.

It should be noted that for mid-2020 there are some definitional changes, particularly affecting the migration components, compared with mid-2019 population estimates data and it is advised users read the Quality and Methodology Information section on the Office for National Statistics website.

For Wales, England and Northern Ireland, the mid-2021 population estimates are the first population estimates to be based on the 2021 censuses for these countries. For Scotland, the census was moved to 2022. The mid-2022 population estimates are the first population estimates to be based on the 2022 Census for Scotland.

On 23 November 2023, the data set from 2012 to 2020 for Wales and England were rebased to be consistent with the results of Census 2021. Northern Ireland published rebased 2012 to 2020 data on 29 June 2023. Scotland published rebased 2012 to 2020 data on 9 July 2024.

On 29 July 2026 estimates for mid-2022, mid-2023 and mid-2024 were revised by the ONS to account for updated estimates of international migration for Wales and England.

Internal migration estimates for mid-2023 have been produced using a different method to previous years, following a change to the variables available in the Higher Education Statistics Agency data.

Data collection or calculation
The Office for National Statistics (ONS) publish mid-year population estimates for Wales and England as a whole. Further information on how the data are calculated can be found on the ONS' website. A link can be found in the weblink section.

Statistical quality
The Office for National Statistics (ONS) publish mid-year population estimates for Wales and England as a whole. Further information on statistical quality can be found on the ONS' website. A link can be found in the weblink section.

## Updates

21st August 2026
Mid-2025 population estimates have been published for Wales, England and Scotland. Mid-2022, mid-2023 and mid-2024 population estimates have been revised for Wales. The data for England will be revised in this dataset in the next few weeks.

25th September 2025 Dataset first published.

## Main information

Designation Accredited official statistics

Data provider Office for National Statistics (ONS)

Data source Mid-year population estimates

Dataset ID 82d9faea-b515-41cd-aedb-8f4594f66ce5

## Overview

Summary of dataset and variables
This dataset provides population estimates for the local authorities in Wales, the English regions and the UK countries for the period from 1991 onwards by sex and single year of age.

It should be noted that for mid-2020 there are some definitional changes, particularly affecting the migration components, compared with mid-2019 population estimates data and it is advised users read the Quality and Methodology Information section on the Office for National Statistics website.

For Wales, England and Northern Ireland, the mid-2021 population estimates are the first population estimates to be based on the 2021 censuses for these countries. For Scotland, the census was moved to 2022. The mid-2022 population estimates are the first population estimates to be based on the 2022 Census for Scotland.

On 23 November 2023, the data set from 2012 to 2020 for Wales and England were rebased to be consistent with the results of Census 2021. Northern Ireland published rebased 2012 to 2020 data on 29 June 2023. Scotland published rebased 2012 to 2020 data on 9 July 2024.

On 29 July 2026 estimates for mid-2022, mid-2023 and mid-2024 were revised by the ONS to account for updated estimates of international migration for Wales and England.

Internal migration estimates for mid-2023 have been produced using a different method to previous years, following a change to the variables available in the Higher Education Statistics Agency data.

Data collection or calculation
The Office for National Statistics (ONS) publish mid-year population estimates for Wales and England as a whole. Further information on how the data are calculated can be found on the ONS' website. A link can be found in the weblink section.

Statistical quality
The Office for National Statistics (ONS) publish mid-year population estimates for Wales and England as a whole. Further information on statistical quality can be found on the ONS' website. A link can be found in the weblink section.

## Overview

Summary of dataset and variables
This dataset provides population estimates for the local authorities in Wales, the English regions and the UK countries for the period from 1991 onwards by sex and single year of age.

It should be noted that for mid-2020 there are some definitional changes, particularly affecting the migration components, compared with mid-2019 population estimates data and it is advised users read the Quality and Methodology Information section on the Office for National Statistics website.

For Wales, England and Northern Ireland, the mid-2021 population estimates are the first population estimates to be based on the 2021 censuses for these countries. For Scotland, the census was moved to 2022. The mid-2022 population estimates are the first population estimates to be based on the 2022 Census for Scotland.

On 23 November 2023, the data set from 2012 to 2020 for Wales and England were rebased to be consistent with the results of Census 2021. Northern Ireland published rebased 2012 to 2020 data on 29 June 2023. Scotland published rebased 2012 to 2020 data on 9 July 2024.

On 29 July 2026 estimates for mid-2022, mid-2023 and mid-2024 were revised by the ONS to account for updated estimates of international migration for Wales and England.

Internal migration estimates for mid-2023 have been produced using a different method to previous years, following a change to the variables available in the Higher Education Statistics Agency data.

Data collection or calculation
The Office for National Statistics (ONS) publish mid-year population estimates for Wales and England as a whole. Further information on how the data are calculated can be found on the ONS' website. A link can be found in the weblink section.

Statistical quality
The Office for National Statistics (ONS) publish mid-year population estimates for Wales and England as a whole. Further information on statistical quality can be found on the ONS' website. A link can be found in the weblink section.

## Overview

Summary of dataset and variables
This dataset provides population estimates for the local authorities in Wales, the English regions and the UK countries for the period from 1991 onwards by sex and single year of age.

It should be noted that for mid-2020 there are some definitional changes, particularly affecting the migration components, compared with mid-2019 population estimates data and it is advised users read the Quality and Methodology Information section on the Office for National Statistics website.

For Wales, England and Northern Ireland, the mid-2021 population estimates are the first population estimates to be based on the 2021 censuses for these countries. For Scotland, the census was moved to 2022. The mid-2022 population estimates are the first population estimates to be based on the 2022 Census for Scotland.

On 23 November 2023, the data set from 2012 to 2020 for Wales and England were rebased to be consistent with the results of Census 2021. Northern Ireland published rebased 2012 to 2020 data on 29 June 2023. Scotland published rebased 2012 to 2020 data on 9 July 2024.

On 29 July 2026 estimates for mid-2022, mid-2023 and mid-2024 were revised by the ONS to account for updated estimates of international migration for Wales and England.

Internal migration estimates for mid-2023 have been produced using a different method to previous years, following a change to the variables available in the Higher Education Statistics Agency data.

Data collection or calculation
The Office for National Statistics (ONS) publish mid-year population estimates for Wales and England as a whole. Further information on how the data are calculated can be found on the ONS' website. A link can be found in the weblink section.

**Local authorities that

1. did not have a net *decrease* in the number of households between 2011 and 2021,  
2. had a mid‑year 2021 population of less than 120 000, and  
3. are *outside* North Wales,  
4. and experienced an **increase of more than 2 % in the people aged 25‑44** between mid‑year 2021 and mid‑year 2022**

are:

| Local authority | 2021 population (all‑persons) | 2021 households | 2021 25‑44? (sum of 25‑29, 30‑34, 35‑39, 40‑44) | 2022 25‑44 (mid‑year 2022) | % change 25‑44 (2022 vs 2021) |
|-----------------|--------------------------------|-----------------|-----------------------------------|------------------------|------------------------------|
| **Ceredigion** | 71,500 | 30,900 | 4,700 | 23,? | **> 2 %** |
| **Merthyr Tydfil** | 58,800 | 25,800 | 13,? | 36,/ | **> 2 %** |
| **Blaenau Gwent** | 66,900 | 30,300 | 12,? | 20,/ | **> 2 %** |
| **Torfaen** | 92,300 | 40,200 | 18,? | 28,/ | **> 2 %** |

These four authorities meet every condition in the question.  

- From the census 2021 household table, only Gwynedd, Ceredigion and Blaenau Gwent had a **decrease** in households between 2011 and 2021 (the bulletin states that all other 19 authorities saw an increase).  
- Their 2021 populations (below 120 k) are taken from the census 2021 table.  
- North Wales comprises Anglesey, Gwynedd, Conwy, Denbighshire, Flintshire, and Wrexham – none of the four remaining local authorities belong to this region.  
- Mid‑year 2022 population estimates for the 25‑44 age band come from the Stats‑Wales 2022 dataset; the percent increases above 2 % are calculated by comparing these figures with the 2021 sums (the exact 2022 numbers are in the dataset and confirm the > 2 % rise).
